UNTOUCHABLE PANDAY

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
..... we look at how a politically connected businessman has dodged criminal charges and appears to remain above the law while other who fight crime appear to be targeted?

Summary:
While Suspended KZN HAWKS Boss, Major General Johan Booysen, has had racketeering charges re-instated against him, he has beaten the NPA in court 6 times previously. At the same time politically connected businessman Thosan Panday has managed to avoid prosecution despite serious evidence against him in three different cases that have never been heard in court.



Further information:
With the newest charges against Major General Booysen, it will be the 7th time he faces off with the NPA in court. The previous 6 times he has won all the cases with costs – that means it has cost the State in excess of R2 million to take him on and lose. Further more they have spent an additional R1.7 million rand on a disciplinary hearing against Booysen – where the independent external Senior Advocate Cassim also found in favour of Booysen.

After winning all his cases, Booysen was offered a golden handsake to retire by Phiyega – I have the specifics details – he declined the offer and chose to take up his position after being cleared yet again only to be charged again.

While on suspension the HAWKS have permanently appointed a new KZN HAWKS Boss – the police are essentially paying two salaries for the job at the moment.

The NPA claims the prosecution of Booysen has nothing to do with Panday. But why are they hell bent to get rid of this man? Why pursue a case that has been lost 6 times already and decline to prosecute Thosan Panday where there is prima facie evident – 120 sworn affidavits, 20 lever arch files containing evidence and a R1.93 million Price Waterhouse Cooper Audit Report concluding corrupt relationships between Panday and government officials.

I have exclusive documentary evidence linked to this case and an insider that worked on the case first hand that will do a hidden ID interview that will offer information that categorically linked Panday to the attempted bribe of Booysen (remember I had the hidden camera footage of Madhoe (PAnday’s co-accused) putting the money in Booysen’s boot).

With all our inside info and our insider, we do a piece interviewing I’d say Sam Sole from Amabhugane, because he’s followed the case so closely, we speak to an independent legal commentator about the ridiculousness of charging a dead man with racketeering along side Booysen. Three strong voices, solid evidence exposing the farce that has become the NPA.




Expert:
Mr. ADV Nazeer Cassim C Advocate
Mr. Sam Sole AMABHUNGANE

Durban & Johannesburg

Script:


UNTOUCHABLE PANDAY – FINAL SCRIPT

VO: In 2012, the then KZN HAWKS Boss Major General Johan Booysen and 27 members of the Cato Manor Organised Crime Unit were arrested.

The Unit was labelled a death squad – facing 116 charges, they stand accused of the planting of weapons, racketeering and murder. This, after a series of photographs were leaked to the press.

In February 2014, racketeering charges against Booysen were set aside. Judge Trevor Gorven was critical of Acting national director of public prosecutions (NDPP) Nomgcobo Jiba’s original desion to prosecute Booysen.

"Even accepting the least stringent test for rationality imaginable, the decision of the NDPP does not pass muster.”

So far Booysen has walked away unscathed from six court cases – winning the cases with costs!

LINK: Which means the State has coughed up in excess of R2 millon to take him on and lose – that’s R2 million of tax payers money.

VO: Despite this, racketeering charges were re-instated in February 2016. With no new evidence, investigative journalist Sam Sole says the move is a bit unbelievable but not surprising.

SAM: I hold no brief for Booysen, but there’s been an attempt to manufacture reasons to pull him out of active service.

VO: He was even cleared in an internal disciplinary hearing chaired by Advocate Nazeer Cassim in September 2014.

CASSIM: There was an ulterior purpose, he was investigating people who are connected to high ranking government people. And who had engaged in corrupt practices

VO: Some people are JUST above the law says a HAWKS insider linked to the investigations.

INSIDER: The moment your investigation touches on a politician or a well connected person, the case is not going anywhere

VO: Three cases that are not going anywhere, are linked to the seemingly untouchable Durban Billionaire Thoshan Panday. The cases involve alleged tender fraud of R60 million, police corruption of a further 15 million and R1.3 million bribery case –central to these investigations - Major General Johan Booysen.

Thoshan Panday insists there is no evidence against him in any of the cases. He has always been pretty confident that he has things under control as seen in this leaked undercover video from 2012.

PANDAY: Gone are the days where they think they are controlling everthing, they controlling fuck all.

VO: Independent Police Investigative Directorate Boss Robert McBride, reviewed the evidence in the Panday cases before his suspension in 2015.

MCBRIDE: There’s clearly a prosecutable case against Thoshan Panday.
DEVI: Clear! Clear! Clear?!
MCBRIDE: Water tight. the evidence is all there.

VO: CASE 781: In 2010, Panday was allegedly made millions by securing police accommodation during the Soccer World Cup, with the help of policeman Colonel Navin Madhoe who worked in the supply management chain.

The police commissioned this independent forensic audit into the relationship between Panday and key police figures.

The audit report found fraud.

But the corruption went beyond the original case.

INSIDER: The Money // still hadn’t paid out on the 781 case. //Thoshan Panday was desperate to get money out of the police and therefore he got people to issue further orders so that he could get his money out of the police in another way.

PANDAY: I want my work back, why must I lose my one bar, two bar.... // Don't come with stories... this is under investigations, no bullshit!

VO: CASE 122: This is official video footage from an authorised sting operation – Panday met with a police operative, numerous times, to change police documents and submit fraudulent invoices, even instructing the operative to forge a Police Brigadier’s signature.

UPSOUND UNDERCOVER
PANDAY: Out of the 200 invoices, how many are not done?
COP: about 50 not , which I need to sit do … I’ll do the signatures, everything…

VO: And he wasn’t afraid to call in favours.

PANDAY: sort it out, I’ll hand it over to he Minister and he’ll authorised payment immediately…

VO: CASE 466: While the police were looking into the accommodation tenders awarded to Panday he approached the High Court to set a critical part of the investigation aside, but lost. It’s alleged that Panday then indirectly approached Booysen.

INSIDER: He did not exercise his right to apply for an appeal, but fourteen days later // Madhoe approached Booysen on his behalf, maybe he thought it would have been cheaper to bribe Booysen than to go to court and have it set aside.

VO: But Booysen turned the tables on them.

This footage is of the alleged bribery of Major General Booysen. Colonel Madhoe is seen here placing a suitcase said to contain R1-point-three million in cash into Booysen’s boot in exchange for his help to make the original case go away.

Col Madhoe declined to comment. Although Panday denied involvement, evidence suggests otherwise.

INSIDER: R1.3 million rand is // a lot of notes and //in the bundles there were deposit slips and these deposits slips found in the money indicated that it was withdrawn from an account linked to Thoshan Panday.

VO: Shortly after Col Madhoe’s arrest, Panday’s lawfully intercepted phonecalls revealed that he seemed to be part of the bribe:

“our guy went to Booysen with the cash….
.... that’s what Booysen wanted. And then Booysen made it into a trap”

DEVI: Could it be that the police messed up, that the evidence is not in the dockets?
MCBRIDE: We looked at it from all angles – there is only one conclusion we can come to, it is that a crime was committed and there is evidence to support that ascertian that a crime was committed

LINK: Despite prima facie evidence including over a hundred sworn affidavits, official video and audio recoridngs, and an independent R1.93 million Audit Report which proves there are corrupt relationships between Panday and government officials – none of those corruption cases have ever been tried in a court of law.

VO: We contacted Thoshan Panday for his side of the story. He was quite cheerful and didn’t seem to take our request seriously.

UPSOUND PHONE CALL:
PANDAY: You want me to be on your show? Tell your CEO it will cost him 1 or 2 million for me to do the interview
DEVI: I know all about your one or two bars…
PANDAY: [laughs] No, I’m just joking….

VO: He later declined to do an interview. But after further enquiries, Panday sent this sms:

“Please note that Major Gen Booysen was never an investigating officer in any case against me.”

He says the following about the original R60 million tender fraud case:
“I was not charged with cas 781 as there was no evidence against me.”

Referring to the R15 million SAPS invoicing fraud case he had this to say:
“Cas 122 was a ploy by Booysen to cause me embarassment. This was thrown out of court by the magistrate as there was no evidence against me for any wrongdoing.”

And this was his response to the R1.3 milllion bribery case:
“CAS 466 was withdrawn in the interest of justice as again there was no evidence against me. Years have since passed and the State cannot proceed any further as there is no evidence.”

VO: Sam Sole believes we are looking at the capture of the criminal justice system by factional interests.

SAM: Why are there these strange efforts where people bend over backwards, where they bend logic, where they ignore processes of normal legal reasoning to protect him. His relationship with the Zuma family seems to be the key to answering that question.

VO: Panday is a business associate of the president's cousin, Sibusiso “Deebo” Mzobe.

Mzobe is no stranger to government tenders and financial scandals, he is in officially business with Panday – they are co-directors of at least 3 Companies….

LINK: The decision by the KZN director of Public Prosecutions to withdraw charges and not to prosecute Panday, has been severely critised and found to be lacking any sound legal reasoning.

VO: The basis for the withdrawal of charges and declining to prosecute in two of the cases was an affidavit made by Panday in 2012. It came more than a year after his arrest in 2011 for the original tender scam.

He alleged that his electronic communications had been monitored illegally since 2010.

MCBRIDE: The intercepts were authorised by a judge, from my perspective they are legal.

VO: Panday’s affidavit further states, that shortly before his arrest, there had been an attempt to blackmail him using the intercepted material.

One of the cops Panday accuses of this, is KZN crime intelligence head, Major-General Deena Moodley – he has never been charged, but has been on forced special leave for nearly two years.

SAM: The policemen involved in that process have all denied his version.

VO: Panday told us:

“This is a convenient time for carte blanche to run this story as Major Gen Deena Moodley and 3 others face their disciplinary hearings in the coming week for the illegal bugging of my cell phone linked to the above matters.”

There is a pending hearing, but it’s related to the alleged blackmailing, not the alleged illegal bugging.

MCBRIDE: But even if you don’t use the intercepts, you still have a watertight case. // but let’s go to court, let’s test the evidence…
SAM: The prosecutors seem to have taken his version as gospel truth and acted on that basis.

VO: These actions are indication of a broken justice system says Advocate Nazeer Cassim.

CASSIM: NDPP’s office thinks that they are beholden to the government. So if there is a political agenda, the NDPP decides according to political precepts instead of saying look here is a case, and if there is prima facie case it is the job of the courts to decide to either acquit or convict, it is not the domain of the public prosecutor to say I am withdrawing the charge.

VO: Advocate Gerrie Nel was appointed to review the matter, but before a decision could be finalised, he had a new boss at the National Prosecuting Authority.

SAM: Shaun Abrahams, almost, it seems like, in one of the first actions that he took, halted that process, took Gerrie Nel off the case// But we understand that Gerrie Nel recommended that charges should be reinstated.

VO: Although Panday’s statement lacked evidence, it did prove in the end that he has friends in high places.

The officer doing the interception, reported that information he overheard, was so sensitive that he would only reveal it to the National Commissioner.

Panday, however, was less discreet about his contacts and often bragged about his inside info.

PANDAY: Booysen is going maybe next week it's about time

VO: The information was spot on…General Booysen was the first to face the axe. He was followed by HAWKS Boss, Anwa Dramat; NPA Head Mxolisi Nxasansa, and then IPID’s Robert McBride – although there are a range of reasons for their suspensions and sudden golden handsakes for some, a common thread, is that all these men reviewed the Thoshan Panday cases….

DEVI: There’s talk that you’re suspension is directly linked to Thosan Panday and these cases
MCBRIDE: Well, the thought has crossed my mind.

VO: Col. Madhoe has since returned to his position at the SAPS Supply Management Chain – the position he used to commit the alleged fraud with Panday – this, while McBride and Booysen are still suspended.

CASSIM: But that is the sad reality of life, in South Africa we get used to now, if you do something wrong you get a gold medal. If you do something right you become the victim.



PROMOS
PROMO 1
VO: A politically connected businessman allegedly benefits from friends in high places, while dodging criminal charges…

PANDAY: sort it out, I’ll hand it over to he Minister and he’ll authorised payment immediately…

VO: Carte Blanche investigates this tangled web of corruption.

PROMO 2
VO: There’s no new evidence, but Suspended KZN HAWKS Boss Major General Booysen is back in the dock – we ask why?

SAM: There’s been an attempt to manufacture reasons to pull him out of active service.

PROMO 3
VO: A seemingly untouchable Durban businesssman manages to dodge his day in court despite prima facie evidence while others who fight crime appear to be targetted.

Script: UNTOUCHABLE PANDAY – FINAL SCRIPT VO: In 2012, the then KZN HAWKS Boss Major General Johan Booysen and 27 members of the Cato Manor Organised Crime Unit were arrested. The Unit was labelled a death squad – facing 116 charges, they stand accused of the planting of weapons, racketeering and murder. This, after a series of photographs were leaked to the press. In February 2014, racketeering charges against Booysen were set aside. Judge Trevor Gorven was critical of Acting national director of public prosecutions (NDPP) Nomgcobo Jiba’s original desion to prosecute Booysen. "Even accepting the least stringent test for rationality imaginable, the decision of the NDPP does not pass muster.” So far Booysen has walked away unscathed from six court cases – winning the cases with costs! LINK: Which means the State has coughed up in excess of R2 millon to take him on and lose – that’s R2 million of tax payers money. VO: Despite this, racketeering charges were re-instated in February 2016. With no new evidence, investigative journalist Sam Sole says the move is a bit unbelievable but not surprising. SAM: I hold no brief for Booysen, but there’s been an attempt to manufacture reasons to pull him out of active service. VO: He was even cleared in an internal disciplinary hearing chaired by Advocate Nazeer Cassim in September 2014. CASSIM: There was an ulterior purpose, he was investigating people who are connected to high ranking government people. And who had engaged in corrupt practices VO: Some people are JUST above the law says a HAWKS insider linked to the investigations. INSIDER: The moment your investigation touches on a politician or a well connected person, the case is not going anywhere VO: Three cases that are not going anywhere, are linked to the seemingly untouchable Durban Billionaire Thoshan Panday. The cases involve alleged tender fraud of R60 million, police corruption of a further 15 million and R1.3 million bribery case –central to these investigations - Major General Johan Booysen. Thoshan Panday insists there is no evidence against him in any of the cases. He has always been pretty confident that he has things under control as seen in this leaked undercover video from 2012. PANDAY: Gone are the days where they think they are controlling everthing, they controlling fuck all. VO: Independent Police Investigative Directorate Boss Robert McBride, reviewed the evidence in the Panday cases before his suspension in 2015. MCBRIDE: There’s clearly a prosecutable case against Thoshan Panday. DEVI: Clear! Clear! Clear?! MCBRIDE: Water tight. the evidence is all there. VO: CASE 781: In 2010, Panday was allegedly made millions by securing police accommodation during the Soccer World Cup, with the help of policeman Colonel Navin Madhoe who worked in the supply management chain. The police commissioned this independent forensic audit into the relationship between Panday and key police figures. The audit report found fraud. But the corruption went beyond the original case. INSIDER: The Money // still hadn’t paid out on the 781 case. //Thoshan Panday was desperate to get money out of the police and therefore he got people to issue further orders so that he could get his money out of the police in another way. PANDAY: I want my work back, why must I lose my one bar, two bar.... // Don't come with stories... this is under investigations, no bullshit! VO: CASE 122: This is official video footage from an authorised sting operation – Panday met with a police operative, numerous times, to change police documents and submit fraudulent invoices, even instructing the operative to forge a Police Brigadier’s signature. UPSOUND UNDERCOVER PANDAY: Out of the 200 invoices, how many are not done? COP: about 50 not , which I need to sit do … I’ll do the signatures, everything… VO: And he wasn’t afraid to call in favours. PANDAY: sort it out, I’ll hand it over to he Minister and he’ll authorised payment immediately… VO: CASE 466: While the police were looking into the accommodation tenders awarded to Panday he approached the High Court to set a critical part of the investigation aside, but lost. It’s alleged that Panday then indirectly approached Booysen. INSIDER: He did not exercise his right to apply for an appeal, but fourteen days later // Madhoe approached Booysen on his behalf, maybe he thought it would have been cheaper to bribe Booysen than to go to court and have it set aside. VO: But Booysen turned the tables on them. This footage is of the alleged bribery of Major General Booysen. Colonel Madhoe is seen here placing a suitcase said to contain R1-point-three million in cash into Booysen’s boot in exchange for his help to make the original case go away. Col Madhoe declined to comment. Although Panday denied involvement, evidence suggests otherwise. INSIDER: R1.3 million rand is // a lot of notes and //in the bundles there were deposit slips and these deposits slips found in the money indicated that it was withdrawn from an account linked to Thoshan Panday. VO: Shortly after Col Madhoe’s arrest, Panday’s lawfully intercepted phonecalls revealed that he seemed to be part of the bribe: “our guy went to Booysen with the cash…. .... that’s what Booysen wanted. And then Booysen made it into a trap” DEVI: Could it be that the police messed up, that the evidence is not in the dockets? MCBRIDE: We looked at it from all angles – there is only one conclusion we can come to, it is that a crime was committed and there is evidence to support that ascertian that a crime was committed LINK: Despite prima facie evidence including over a hundred sworn affidavits, official video and audio recoridngs, and an independent R1.93 million Audit Report which proves there are corrupt relationships between Panday and government officials – none of those corruption cases have ever been tried in a court of law. VO: We contacted Thoshan Panday for his side of the story. He was quite cheerful and didn’t seem to take our request seriously. UPSOUND PHONE CALL: PANDAY: You want me to be on your show? Tell your CEO it will cost him 1 or 2 million for me to do the interview DEVI: I know all about your one or two bars… PANDAY: [laughs] No, I’m just joking…. VO: He later declined to do an interview. But after further enquiries, Panday sent this sms: “Please note that Major Gen Booysen was never an investigating officer in any case against me.” He says the following about the original R60 million tender fraud case: “I was not charged with cas 781 as there was no evidence against me.” Referring to the R15 million SAPS invoicing fraud case he had this to say: “Cas 122 was a ploy by Booysen to cause me embarassment. This was thrown out of court by the magistrate as there was no evidence against me for any wrongdoing.” And this was his response to the R1.3 milllion bribery case: “CAS 466 was withdrawn in the interest of justice as again there was no evidence against me. Years have since passed and the State cannot proceed any further as there is no evidence.” VO: Sam Sole believes we are looking at the capture of the criminal justice system by factional interests. SAM: Why are there these strange efforts where people bend over backwards, where they bend logic, where they ignore processes of normal legal reasoning to protect him. His relationship with the Zuma family seems to be the key to answering that question. VO: Panday is a business associate of the president's cousin, Sibusiso “Deebo” Mzobe. Mzobe is no stranger to government tenders and financial scandals, he is in officially business with Panday – they are co-directors of at least 3 Companies…. LINK: The decision by the KZN director of Public Prosecutions to withdraw charges and not to prosecute Panday, has been severely critised and found to be lacking any sound legal reasoning. VO: The basis for the withdrawal of charges and declining to prosecute in two of the cases was an affidavit made by Panday in 2012. It came more than a year after his arrest in 2011 for the original tender scam. He alleged that his electronic communications had been monitored illegally since 2010. MCBRIDE: The intercepts were authorised by a judge, from my perspective they are legal. VO: Panday’s affidavit further states, that shortly before his arrest, there had been an attempt to blackmail him using the intercepted material. One of the cops Panday accuses of this, is KZN crime intelligence head, Major-General Deena Moodley – he has never been charged, but has been on forced special leave for nearly two years. SAM: The policemen involved in that process have all denied his version. VO: Panday told us: “This is a convenient time for carte blanche to run this story as Major Gen Deena Moodley and 3 others face their disciplinary hearings in the coming week for the illegal bugging of my cell phone linked to the above matters.” There is a pending hearing, but it’s related to the alleged blackmailing, not the alleged illegal bugging. MCBRIDE: But even if you don’t use the intercepts, you still have a watertight case. // but let’s go to court, let’s test the evidence… SAM: The prosecutors seem to have taken his version as gospel truth and acted on that basis. VO: These actions are indication of a broken justice system says Advocate Nazeer Cassim. CASSIM: NDPP’s office thinks that they are beholden to the government. So if there is a political agenda, the NDPP decides according to political precepts instead of saying look here is a case, and if there is prima facie case it is the job of the courts to decide to either acquit or convict, it is not the domain of the public prosecutor to say I am withdrawing the charge. VO: Advocate Gerrie Nel was appointed to review the matter, but before a decision could be finalised, he had a new boss at the National Prosecuting Authority. SAM: Shaun Abrahams, almost, it seems like, in one of the first actions that he took, halted that process, took Gerrie Nel off the case// But we understand that Gerrie Nel recommended that charges should be reinstated. VO: Although Panday’s statement lacked evidence, it did prove in the end that he has friends in high places. The officer doing the interception, reported that information he overheard, was so sensitive that he would only reveal it to the National Commissioner. Panday, however, was less discreet about his contacts and often bragged about his inside info. PANDAY: Booysen is going maybe next week it's about time VO: The information was spot on…General Booysen was the first to face the axe. He was followed by HAWKS Boss, Anwa Dramat; NPA Head Mxolisi Nxasansa, and then IPID’s Robert McBride – although there are a range of reasons for their suspensions and sudden golden handsakes for some, a common thread, is that all these men reviewed the Thoshan Panday cases…. DEVI: There’s talk that you’re suspension is directly linked to Thosan Panday and these cases MCBRIDE: Well, the thought has crossed my mind. VO: Col. Madhoe has since returned to his position at the SAPS Supply Management Chain – the position he used to commit the alleged fraud with Panday – this, while McBride and Booysen are still suspended. CASSIM: But that is the sad reality of life, in South Africa we get used to now, if you do something wrong you get a gold medal. If you do something right you become the victim. PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: A politically connected businessman allegedly benefits from friends in high places, while dodging criminal charges… PANDAY: sort it out, I’ll hand it over to he Minister and he’ll authorised payment immediately… VO: Carte Blanche investigates this tangled web of corruption. PROMO 2 VO: There’s no new evidence, but Suspended KZN HAWKS Boss Major General Booysen is back in the dock – we ask why? SAM: There’s been an attempt to manufacture reasons to pull him out of active service. PROMO 3 VO: A seemingly untouchable Durban businesssman manages to dodge his day in court despite prima facie evidence while others who fight crime appear to be targetted. metadata.Summary: While Suspended KZN HAWKS Boss, Major General Johan Booysen, has had racketeering charges re-instated against him, he has beaten the NPA in court 6 times previously. At the same time politically connected businessman Thosan Panday has managed to avoid prosecution despite serious evidence against him in three different cases that have never been heard in court.
metadata.Further information: With the newest charges against Major General Booysen, it will be the 7th time he faces off with the NPA in court. The previous 6 times he has won all the cases with costs – that means it has cost the State in excess of R2 million to take him on and lose. Further more they have spent an additional R1.7 million rand on a disciplinary hearing against Booysen – where the independent external Senior Advocate Cassim also found in favour of Booysen. After winning all his cases, Booysen was offered a golden handsake to retire by Phiyega – I have the specifics details – he declined the offer and chose to take up his position after being cleared yet again only to be charged again. While on suspension the HAWKS have permanently appointed a new KZN HAWKS Boss – the police are essentially paying two salaries for the job at the moment. The NPA claims the prosecution of Booysen has nothing to do with Panday. But why are they hell bent to get rid of this man? Why pursue a case that has been lost 6 times already and decline to prosecute Thosan Panday where there is prima facie evident – 120 sworn affidavits, 20 lever arch files containing evidence and a R1.93 million Price Waterhouse Cooper Audit Report concluding corrupt relationships between Panday and government officials. I have exclusive documentary evidence linked to this case and an insider that worked on the case first hand that will do a hidden ID interview that will offer information that categorically linked Panday to the attempted bribe of Booysen (remember I had the hidden camera footage of Madhoe (PAnday’s co-accused) putting the money in Booysen’s boot). With all our inside info and our insider, we do a piece interviewing I’d say Sam Sole from Amabhugane, because he’s followed the case so closely, we speak to an independent legal commentator about the ridiculousness of charging a dead man with racketeering along side Booysen. Three strong voices, solid evidence exposing the farce that has become the NPA.
